issue_context.title: Decreasing the window size below the amount of data sent can prematurely abort the connection
comments: We've moved this issue to the Backlog milestone. This means that it is not going to be worked on for the coming release. We will reassess the backlog following the current release and consider this item at that time. To learn more about our issue management process and to have better expectation regarding different types of issues you can read our [Triage Process](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/TriageProcess.md).
Moving to backlog. This is a low-pri bug, only affects an edge case in the HTTP/2 spec and only sometimes since it's a race.

We are encountering this issue intermittently after we upgraded our service from .NET 6 to 8.
```
crit: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Http2[63]
      The event loop in connection 0HN3R40QVJ560 failed unexpectedly.
      System.ArgumentOutOfRangeException: Specified argument was out of the range of valid values. (Parameter 'length')
         at System.ThrowHelper.ThrowStartOrEndArgumentValidationException(Int64 start)
         at System.Buffers.ReadOnlySequence`1.Slice(Int64 start, Int64 length)
         at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Server.Kestrel.Core.Internal.Http2.Http2FrameWriter.WriteToOutputPipe()
```
Our service is a grpc server that provides streaming calls to transfer large volumes of data. The grpc client in our case is written in C++. After the error, the grpc client is not notified of any errors, and it remains waiting for a response.

review_comments: This does seem to fix it; it *feels* like we're powering over the real problem, though - like one of the values used in either CheckStreamWindow or CheckConnctionWindow is already at a value we should have clamped. Maybe I'm overthinking... I tend to do that, and this has the advantage of simplicity
I vaguely recall that the spec allows the window size to go negative.  I do think it might be helpful to include a comment about when that can happen.
Do we actually want to continue if it's negative/zero or should we short-circuit something?

@amcasey yes, when the window size becomes we (sender) should wait for window update from the receiver, by continuing the code flow will mark as waiting for window updates, as there are still more data to be written. This will also handle the case if the receiver aborts the connection without sending window update.
Added inline comment to describe the change
Crucially, we're only setting a local to 0, right?  Not our actual window size state?

yes, that's correct, only the local is set to 0
the actual window size remains negative
